title: Halting of the Circuit Scan
statement: Let $C$ be a finite acyclic Boolean circuit with $n$ input vertices, gates listed in topological order, and an output vertex among its $n+|C|$ vertices, where $|C|$ is the number of gates. Let $o$ be an oracle whose answer on the binary representation of each natural number $p$, paired with the unary word of length $n$, is the $p$th bit of the circuit encoding, with value false when that bit is out of range. Suppose the input word $w$ encodes a valid instance of the selected task: for the edge task it encodes a pair of canonical binary words, and for the size or type task it encodes one canonical binary word. Suppose also that the decoded target index or indices are $i_v$ and $t_v$, respectively: in the edge task these are the two words’ represented numbers, and otherwise $t_v$ is the represented number. Then the scan machine for that task, started with all three registers zero and no answer, halts with all registers at most the encoding length of $C$. Its answer is the task’s default answer if $t_v<n$; if $t_v\ge n$ and $t_v-n$ indexes a gate of $C$, its answer is true for the size task, is whether that gate has the requested kind for the type task, and is whether its argument list contains $i_v$ for the edge task; if the index is beyond the gate list, its answer is false.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a DAG circuit with input count $n$
The oracle returns the circuit encoding bit at each represented natural number, defaulting to false out of range
The encoded input satisfies the selected task’s validity condition
The encoded input’s target indices are $i_v,t_v$
The initial configuration has start state, all registers zero, and no result
Throughout the run before halting, every register is bounded by the encoding length of $C$
